The inherited guidance identifies the key failure modes: the seed’s gait was already actuator-infeasible, while the prefilled low-effort policy was simply advected out. I’m now comparing the best finite rollout against the instability and low-effort exits, including the common prewarm sheet, before I write the required diagnosis.

The visual-signal skill changed the candidate direction: the best-score seed is the only rollout with upstream motion, but it saturates and ejects laterally; both cap-feasible descendants are swept out downstream in about 16 time units, and the aggressive branch becomes numerically unstable in 1.9. I’m recording a bounded interpolation hypothesis—retain the finite target-bearing structure, but raise the gait toward (not through) the acceleration envelope—before editing the policy.

The single candidate is now in place. A joint-only 300-time-unit envelope probe (not CFD) stayed below all configured caps in zero, constant, and slowly varying bearing cases: maxima were about `19.0/19.7 deg`, `178/135 deg/time`, and `1670/1260 deg/time²`. I’m now distilling the cross-candidate lesson that “cap-feasible” is necessary but not enough—the controller also needs an empirically adequate upstream propulsion floor.

The candidate and both required evidence files are complete. I’m invoking the mandated check-runner now; it will validate the semantic guidance delta, policy contract/schema, and workspace boundary without launching CFD.
